'''''Coincya monensis''''' is a plant [[species]] in the family [[Brassicaceae]]. ''Coincya monensis'' is native to western [[Europe]] and [[Morocco]], but has been introduced in [[North America]].<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250094657 Flora of North America, Vol. 7. Brassicaceae.]</ref>

==Subspecies==

It contains the [[subspecies]]:<ref>[http://wiki.bugwood.org/Coincya_monensis BugwoodWiki (Center for Invasive Species and Ecosystem Health at the University of Georgia): ''Coincya monensis'', last updated 16 May 2012]</ref><ref>[http://www.invasive.org/gist/alert/alrtcoin.html The Global Invasive Species Team Weed Alert: ''Coincya monensis'', Tunyalee Martin/Wildland Invasive Species Team; January 2000.]</ref>

* ''C. monensis'' subsp. ''cheiranthos'' {{au|(Vill.) Aedo, Leadlay & Muñoz Garm.}} (Wallflower Cabbage) — [[France]], [[Germany]] & [[Spain]]
* ''C. monensis'' subsp. ''hispida'' {{au|(Cav.) Leadlay}} — central [[Portugal]] & central Spain
*  [[Coincya monensis subsp. monensis|''C. monensis'' subsp. ''monensis'']] (Isle of Man cabbage) — the [[British Isles]]
* ''C. monensis'' subsp. ''nevadensis'' {{au|(Willk.) Leadlay}} — southern Spain
* ''C. monensis'' subsp. ''orophila'' {{au|(Franco) Aedo, Leadlay & Muñoz Garm.}}<ref>{{EOL|483195|''Coincya monensis'' (L.) Greuter & Burdet|access-date= 29 December 2012}}</ref> — [[Morocco]], Portugal & Spain
* ''C. monensis'' subsp. ''puberula'' {{au|(Pau) Leadlay}} — northern Portugal & northern Spain
*  [[Coincya monensis subsp. recurvata|''C. monensis'' subsp. ''recurvata'']] {{au|(All.) Leadlay}} (Star mustard) — [[United States]]<ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=COMOR USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service(NRCS) PLANTS database: Coincya monensis (L.)
